common_name: Great Star Hydrangea (Starburst-Shaped Floret Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Great Star blooms on new wood, so prune hard in late winter to stimulate strong new growth and maximum flowering.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, giving afternoon shade where summers are hottest. Great Star is unlike any other panicle hydrangea in flower form — instead of the usual small, densely packed florets, each individual sterile flower has four long, narrow, twisted petals radiating outward, giving the loose, airy flower panicles a distinctive spidery, starburst appearance rather than the typical dense cone shape. Blooming white in summer and often picking up pink tones as panicles age into fall, it makes an unusual textural accent among more conventional mophead and panicle hydrangeas. Like other H. paniculata cultivars it blooms on new wood, so prune hard in late winter to a low framework of buds for the strongest flowering; established plants are more sun- and drought-tolerant than bigleaf hydrangeas.

common_name: Sundae Fraise Hydrangea (Compact Strawberry-Pink Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Sundae Fraise is a compact panicle hydrangea, smaller than Vanilla Strawberry, that fits foundation plantings and smaller gardens.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, giving afternoon shade where summers are hottest. Sundae Fraise produces upright, conical flower panicles that open creamy white in midsummer and gradually flush from the base upward through pink to a rich strawberry-red as the season progresses, giving a bicolor effect similar to the larger Vanilla Strawberry but on a more compact, three-dimensional, well-branched shrub better suited to smaller yards and foundation plantings. Its strong stems hold the panicles upright without flopping even as they mature and gain weight. Like other H. paniculata cultivars it blooms on new wood, so prune hard in late winter to a low framework to encourage vigorous new growth and the largest flower panicles the following summer.

common_name: Diamond Rouge Hydrangea (Deep Red Fall-Color Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Diamond Rouge is selected for panicles that mature to an unusually deep, saturated red rather than the more common pink.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, giving afternoon shade where summers are hottest. Diamond Rouge opens creamy white in midsummer, then deepens through pink to an unusually saturated, dark rose-red by late summer and into fall, a richer, more intense red than most panicle hydrangea cultivars achieve, on sturdy, upright stems that support the dense conical panicles without staking. The strong color development is most pronounced with cooler night temperatures in late summer, so fall color tends to be more dramatic than midsummer color. Like other H. paniculata cultivars it blooms on new wood, so prune hard in late winter to a low, well-spaced framework of buds to encourage vigorous new growth and the largest, most colorful panicles.

common_name: Berry White Hydrangea (Large White-to-Rose-Red Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Berry White bears large, dense flower panicles on strong stems that hold up without flopping even as color deepens and the panicles gain weight.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, giving afternoon shade where summers are hottest. Berry White produces large, dense, conical flower panicles that open pure white in midsummer and gradually flush to a deep rose-red as they mature into fall, giving a full season of two-toned color on the same shrub as older and newer flowers open at different rates along each panicle. Its sturdy, well-branched stems support the heavy flower heads upright through summer storms far better than older seedling-grown panicle hydrangeas. Like other H. paniculata cultivars it blooms reliably on new wood, so prune hard in late winter to a low framework to encourage vigorous new growth and maximize the size and color of the following summer's panicles.

common_name: Polar Bear Hydrangea (Extra-Large White Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Polar Bear is one of the largest-growing panicle hydrangeas, producing very large, sturdy white panicles on a vigorous, upright shrub.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, allowing ample room for its large mature size. Polar Bear grows into one of the biggest panicle hydrangeas commonly available, a vigorous, upright shrub topped from midsummer into fall with very large, dense, pure white conical flower panicles on stout stems strong enough to hold the heavy blooms upright without staking. Its scale suits it to use as a specimen, informal hedge, or screen where a large-growing flowering shrub is wanted, rather than tighter foundation plantings better served by compact panicle cultivars. Like other H. paniculata cultivars it blooms reliably on new wood, so prune hard in late winter to a sturdy low framework to encourage vigorous new growth and the largest panicles the following summer.
